title: Dashboard screenshots attached to reports and pull requests
summary: When a run finishes, SwarmForge captures screenshots of the dashboard tabs affected by the change and uploads them to the draft pull request, so reviewers can see the UI result without opening the dashboard. The run report lists each screenshot (tab, theme and file path).
benefit: Reviewers no longer need to start the dashboard to verify UI changes; the evidence travels with the PR and the report.
where: Draft PR '📸 Visual evidence' section and the 'Visual evidence' section of report.md

title: Plan improvements to SwarmForge itself
summary: Start an improvement project with the SwarmForge repository selected. Use the kickoff chat to agree on milestones, checks and a budget before launching.
benefit: Plan a larger improvement across several milestones and track the resulting tasks on Work.

title: Build an app through milestones
summary: Start with a kickoff conversation, review a written spec, then launch a project that plans from the real repository after each merged task. Milestone reports give you checkpoints to review and correct the direction.
benefit: You can guide a whole app without managing a long list of tasks planned on assumptions.

title: Keep track of new features
summary: Browse feature highlights by date, search by topic, and see where each feature lives in the app. Mark highlights as read when you have caught up.
benefit: You can understand what changed without reading Git commits or remembering every development task.

title: A cleaner SwarmForge workspace
summary: Your hive artwork now appears in the sidebar and welcome screen. Orange accents, clearer spacing and task summary cards make the Work page easier to scan on desktop and phone.
benefit: Spot running work, upcoming tasks and items needing attention at a glance.

title: Faster chat actions and quieter tool details
summary: Use slash shortcuts and pasted URLs to get to common chat actions. Tool activity can be expanded when you need the details, and tools can be turned on or off.
benefit: Move through routine questions with less typing and less transcript clutter.

title: Let chat inspect a workspace safely
summary: Optional file reading, search and command tools run against a read-only workspace in an isolated Docker container. Shell commands are disabled by default.
benefit: Investigate code and failures from the conversation while keeping workspace files protected.
where: Chat; enable chatbot.enable_shell in configuration when needed

title: Compare teams using stronger evidence
summary: Expanded benchmark comparisons track repeated runs, cost and completion outcomes. Delivery and review policy now make missing test evidence and incomplete delivery clearer.
benefit: Choose team settings based on measured results and understand why a run was held.

title: See chat tools working live
summary: Chat can list repository files and show tool calls while an answer is being prepared. Each conversation keeps its own history.
benefit: See what the assistant is checking instead of waiting on an unexplained pause.

title: Follow one task across its retries
summary: Work groups retries under a single task by default. Turn on Every attempt to inspect the earlier runs. Held PRs can get immediate fix-up runs.
benefit: The task list is easier to follow when the swarm repairs its own work.

title: Catch unexpected visual changes
summary: Golden screenshot comparisons can block publication when a visual regression exceeds the configured threshold. CLI commands manage baseline screenshots and comparisons.
benefit: UI changes are checked against an established appearance, alongside code tests.
where: Run review evidence; CLI: swarmforge visual regress / update-golden

title: Clearer delivery failures
summary: Local branch delivery retries its push and reports when delivery did not succeed.
benefit: A finished run no longer hides a failed attempt to deliver its code.

title: Check layouts at phone, tablet and desktop widths
summary: A responsive-layout check screenshots a dashboard tab at 375, 768 and 1280 pixel viewports and inspects the DOM for overflowing or clipped elements. Problems are reported as findings that feed the same repair pipeline as other review findings.
benefit: Layout breakage on phones or tablets is caught automatically instead of surfacing during manual inspection.
